engine_name: Blood Pressure Reading Check: ISH 2020 office categories for a single reading (Normal < 130 and < 85; High-normal 130-139 and/or 85-89; Grade 1 140-159 and/or 90-99; Grade 2 >= 160 and/or >= 100, the higher number deciding), ISH home thresholds for a 7-day average of logged readings (within range < 135 and < 85; above threshold >= 135 or >= 85; well above >= 155 or >= 95; daily means first, then the mean of days, at least 3 days, rounded half-up), a frozen urgent level at systolic >= 180 or diastolic >= 120 on any single reading, pregnancy levels (>= 160 or >= 110 urgent; >= 140 or >= 90 same-day; no categories in pregnancy), a low note at systolic < 90 or diastolic < 60, a resting-pulse note at < 40 or > 120, and refusal of impossible readings (a pulse outside 30-220 is left out with the pulse line, never refused: version 1.1, D3-50)
intended_use: Free educational check for adults that places a single blood pressure reading, or a signed-in member's 7-day home average, in the ISH 2020 categories with plain guidance, and shows the frozen urgent-care wording before anything else when a reading reaches the urgent level. The urgent wording is free for everyone, always, on the calculator and on the logging screen. It does not diagnose high blood pressure; a single reading is a snapshot and nothing here replaces a doctor's assessment.
eligibility: Adults aged 18 to 99. Pregnant or not sure: the pregnancy levels and wording are shown and categories are not shown (D3-19). Readings outside systolic 60-260, diastolic 30-160, or diastolic not at least 10 below systolic are refused with no category; a pulse outside 30-220 is left out (not saved) and the reading checked as usual (D3-50). Members taking blood pressure medicine see the treated-reading wording; the category is unchanged. The 7-day average needs readings on at least 3 different days in the 7 calendar days ending today.
sources: Unger T, et al. 2020 International Society of Hypertension global hypertension practice guidelines. Hypertension 2020;75:1334-57 and J Hypertens 2020;38:982-1004 (ISH 2020; categories, home thresholds and the urgent level; decision I-08).

Whelton PK, et al. 2017 ACC/AHA guideline. Hypertension 2018;71:e13-115; Jones DW, et al. 2025 AHA/ACC guideline. Circulation 2025 (ACC/AHA 2017, reaffirmed 2025: hypertensive crisis > 180/120; shown in the guidelines-differ note).
NICE NG136 Hypertension in adults (2019, updated 2023) (clinic 140/90, home or ambulatory 135/85; severe >= 180/120; home stage-2 threshold 150/95 behind the 155/95 home grade-2 equivalent).
NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (2019) (hypertension in pregnancy >= 140/90; severe >= 160/110).
Brown MA, et al. ISSHP classification of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Hypertension 2018;72:24-43 (ISSHP 2018; pregnancy levels).
ACOG 2020 (pregnancy levels, cited in the sign-off record as a basis for D3-19).
McEvoy JW, et al. 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of elevated blood pressure and hypertension. Eur Heart J 2024;45:3912-4018 (guidelines-differ note).
Mancia G, et al. 2023 ESH Guidelines. J Hypertens 2023;41:1874-2071 (guidelines-differ note).
Stergiou GS, et al. 2021 ESH practice guidelines for office and out-of-office blood pressure measurement. J Hypertens 2021;39:1293-302 (home protocol).
WHO guideline for the pharmacological treatment of hypertension in adults (2021) (guidelines-differ note).
limitations: A single reading is a snapshot: blood pressure moves with activity, stress, caffeine and time of day.
Home monitors need the right cuff size and position.
The categories are the ISH 2020 categories; other countries' guidelines differ (US stage 1 starts at 130/80; Europe, the UK and most of the world use 140/90).
The home grade-2 equivalent (155/95) is not in ISH 2020; it is NICE NG136's home stage-2 threshold (150/95) adjusted to ISH's 5 mmHg office-home gap (D3-18).

The 7-day average uses every logged reading (ISH's discard-day-1 rule applies to its structured protocol, which members may not follow); the category is decided on the rounded numbers shown (D55 principle).
Nothing here replaces a doctor's assessment; the member's own doctor's advice comes first.
regulatory_statement: Approved by the owner as clinical reviewer on 3 November 2026 (NFR3-14; D3-16 to D3-21); version 1.1 approved on 4 November 2026 (D3-50). General health information, not a diagnosis or a medical device. The urgent-care level and its exact text are frozen by CI (FR3-46 AS-03) and are never paid for.
